text:
Marco: Quick sync — MerchantPilot POC final readout prep. Need to lock metrics, gaps, and an expansion ask for the execs. 2pm PT today to prep slides?
Priya: I can run the model-level metrics and the eval set summary by noon. Do we have the canonical prompt set?
Marco: @Priya — yes, use the set under `s3://rp-pocs/merchantpilot/prompts/v3.txt`. Focus on refund detection and intent classification prompts.
Priya: Got it. I'll run p50/p95 latency + token cost calc. Target sLO we agreed: p95 < 250ms and cost < $0.09 per 1k tokens for the main flow.
Alex: Security review brief — MerchantPilot raised standard infra questions: KMS for keys, isolation for PII, and SOC2 evidence. I have the answers but need the final list of fields they flagged.
Jen: They flagged order_id, customer_email, and transaction_notes. We're proposing auto-redaction + prefix hashing for order_id in logs.
Sam: Pricing question from the buyer: if they go Dedicated 3x8 GPUs, what's the uplift to list? Short answer we need a committed monthly number. Can someone prep a quick estimate?
Nora: I can model Dedicated vs Hosted. If they commit 3x A10 equivalent monthly we should show committed discount ~25% and reserved capacity SLA. Will send numbers in spreadsheet.
Raj: For success criteria, propose: 1) intent classification F1 >= 0.88 on the eval set, 2) end-to-end latency p95 < 250ms, 3) false positive rate on refund triggers < 3%, 4) stability over 48h under peak traffic. Agree?
Priya: Agree with metrics. I'll attach eval snippet in thread:
```
# sample eval runner
for prompt in prompts_v3:
  out = client.generate(model=\"rwd-llm-13B-infer\", prompt=prompt, max_tokens=128)
  record_metrics(out)
```
Priya: Current eval run (30k prompts): intent F1 = 0.872, refund FPR = 3.4%, latency p95 = 238ms, cost est = $0.095/1k tokens.
Marco: So we're slightly missing F1 and refund FPR. Need remediation plan + content for readout: what caused drift, prompt tweaks, and quantization impact.
Priya: Early signal shows tokenization edge cases on currency symbols and a few merchant-specific phrases. I'll run prompt normalization + one-shot examples and re-eval.
Jen: Ops/infra note — KV cache warmup reduces cold-start latency a lot. We should show a before/after in the readout (first 5 minutes vs steady state).
Alex: Security follow-ups: add KMS key policy snippet, confirm retention window for logs (90 days by default). I'll paste the policy example in the deck.
Sam: Buyer also asked about data residency for EU customers. We need to confirm private deployment options and whether they can route EU traffic to Frankfurt region.
Nora: Yes — we can propose Private (VPC) with region pinning. Add a slide with deployment options + cost delta.
Raj: For the expansion ask, propose: 3-month pilot -> production pilot with Dedicated reserved capacity + training of 2 merchant templates. Ask = $75k committed MRR equivalent for Dedicated reservation. Thoughts?
Marco: Sounds reasonable. Let's make the ask explicit: cost, expected SLA, and projected unit economics (savings per 1M tokens).
Priya: ETA on re-run is 90 minutes. If re-eval hits F1 >= 0.885 and FPR < 3%, we can present as "meets target after prompt normalization".
Jen: I'll prepare the slide with deployment diagram and warmup strategy. Include a snippet showing cache hit rate curve.
Alex: I'll include the security checklist answers and note SOC2 artifacts availability + timeline for any further pen-testing.
ci-bot: build-notify: merchantpilot-eval-run completed (success).
Marco: OK team — agenda for 2pm: 1) final metrics, 2) remediation steps and results, 3) security/compliance answers, 4) pricing & expansion ask, 5) next steps and owners.
Sam: I'll run pricing numbers and put the dedicated vs hosted breakdown in the slide deck.
Nora: I'll draft the executive summary slide with the ask and 3 alternative pricing packages (conservative, balanced, aggressive).
Priya: Re-eval complete: F1 = 0.891, FPR = 2.6%, latency p95 = 245ms, cost = $0.091/1k tokens. Uploading results now.
Marco: Nice work. Confirm owners: Priya -> metrics + eval; Nora -> pricing slide; Alex -> security slide; Jen -> infra/warmup; Sam -> commercial slide + ask.
Raj: I'll join the readout and lead the technical Q&A with the buyer.
Marco: Perfect. See you all at 2pm PT. I'll post the final slide link 15min before. :thumbsup:
